reasoning: Everyday Palestinian formula said when something worrying comes up. The verb is yistur, with i then u.
Collective noun samak for fish; one fish is samake.
ص is emphatic, so capital S. Ordinary Palestinian word for pavement or sidewalk.
Long ii then taa marbuta after ر, which gives a. Used of the historic Palestine pound and of Turkish or Lebanese lira.
b-prefixed 2ms present bti3raf, then the bare subjunctive tsuu' with a glottal ق. Knowing how to do something is expressed with 3irif plus a verb.
حق has a glottal ق doubled by the shadda, so two apostrophes. Taa marbuta after د is e; in a formal speech the same phrase is heard as 7aq il-3awda.
Form X participle on the Palestinian mista- pattern, like mista3jil. The medial hamza is written.
أوضة is the everyday Ramallah word for room and takes -it in a construct, so ooDit. أكل gets an epenthetic vowel: il-akil.
Initial آ is just the long vowel; the hamza after the article is written, il-'usbuu3. Said for the weekend alongside nihaayit il-'usbuu3.
Shadda on ج doubles it. The word on every bakery sign in Ramallah for savoury pastries; some speakers reduce it to m3ajjanaat.
Adjective loses its first short vowel: kbiir, not kabiir. Said to mean things will work out.
From أعان, the subjunctive y3iin plus the 1sg object -ni, which doubles the n after the long vowel. Also heard shortened to allah y3iin.
hoon with long oo; la- is the slot for the destination and the ellipsis is not romanized. قديش has a glottal ق and a doubled د.
ween is the Palestinian where, with long ee. The frame leaves the article attached to whatever noun follows, and the article assimilates to sun letters.
bi- plus the article before the moon letter آ, which is read as the long vowel aa. Common discourse marker for in the end.
ج is a moon letter so the article stays il-. The medial hamza is written: il-jazaa'ir.
ها plus the article fused into hal-, the Palestinian demonstrative proclitic. The hamza after it is written.
Form VIII present, 2ms, with the b-prefix: btishtighil. ween for where, as in Palestinian.
Shadda doubles the l and the ق is a glottal stop. Also means hung something up; the commenting sense is standard in Palestinian.
Long ee, not ay: ba3deen. Very common Palestinian adverb for later or then.
Passive participle mashghuul, said of a busy person and of an engaged phone line.
Form II with shadda on ج. Used both for encouraging someone and for supporting a team.
ح is 7 and ض is emphatic D. Natural in questions like miin 7aDar il-3urs. Note the doubled 7aDDar means prepared.
Long oo, not uu: looz. Collective noun for almonds.
French loan with a long ee in the second syllable. Used in Ramallah beside 7ammaam for the room itself.
